blocks.text: Lots and land in Central Pt Coquitlam
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots: detached homes here are freehold; a fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees. Condos, townhomes and rowhouses in the sub-area are strata titled — built strata stock, not land.
All are built or strata-unit stock, named here only so a land reader does not mistake them for lot inventory.
TENURE RECORD only — Mayfair Terrace, 2266 Atkins Ave: It is an apartment-form strata, recorded here only so its tenure is never mistaken for land stock.
Excluded tenure traps: Kew Lifestyles at Montrose (2430 Mary Hill Rd) is purpose-built 55+ RENTAL — nothing to buy.
ALR edge: ALR land in the city is in the south, including land in and around Colony Farm Regional Park at the central area's west edge.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Central Pt Coquitlam

items.t: Community Port Coquitlam: detached median $1,262,500, $563/sq ft, 97% sale-to-list, 42 days; condos & townhomes median $660,000, $613/sq ft, 95%, 27 days. Land has no SnapStats category — no figure above is a land figure.
That result is for that address only and is non-transferable.

Recreation and trails: the Port Coquitlam Community Centre, with the Terry Fox Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library), is at 2150 Wilson Avenue downtown; Gates Park is at 2300 Reeve Street; the Traboulay PoCo Trail loops the city and runs along the riverfront through the central area, and Colony Farm Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) sits on the Coquitlam River at the city's west edge.

Flood shape: a significant portion of Port Coquitlam is within the Fraser and Pitt River floodplain and is protected by dyke infrastructure, with pump stations and dyke patrols — the low-lying downtown and riverfront lands are part of that floodplain picture, and lot-level status must be checked with the City.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central Pt Coquitlam

items.t: OCP — City of Port Coquitlam Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 3838: which identifies Downtown as a mixed-use neighbourhood developing further in that role.

Zoning — Port Coquitlam Zoning Bylaw No. 3630: apartment zones RA1 (FAR 1.0, increasable to 1.5 where required parking is provided underground or within a structure, and further to 2.0 on payment of a $50/sq ft contribution to City reserve funds for community amenities) and RA2 (FAR up to 2.5), concentrated downtown and along main roads; townhouse zones RTh1, RTh2 and RTh3; a rowhouse zone RRh; and single-detached zones RS1 through RS4. Minimum lot widths for detached lots run from RS1 at least 15 m and RS2 at least 12 m to RS3 at least 30 m and RS4 at least 9.5 m.

SSMUH — Port Coquitlam, as the City states it: RS-zoned lots across the city can hold 3 to 6 small-scale multi-unit housing units without rezoning, depending on lot size, location and transit proximity, and secondary suite rules apply.

Property taxes — City of Port Coquitlam: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on current taxes unpaid after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 15, 2026; the City's 2026 increase was 1.95% for the average home, and the City states it has the lowest average property taxes and utility fees in Metro Vancouver; utility bills are flat annual water and sewer fees, billed separately and due March 31, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central Pt Coquitlam

items.t: Port Coquitlam is Terry Fox's hometown (Nov 1, 2026). Terry Fox grew up in the city; the Terry Fox: Inspiring Local Champions exhibit is at the Port Coquitlam Community Centre, and the Terry Fox Library sits in the same building at 2150 Wilson Avenue.

The downtown community centre is a $132-million rebuild (Oct 2, 2021). The Port Coquitlam Community Centre (2150 Wilson Ave) fully opened Oct 2, 2021 — three arenas, leisure pool, fitness centre, Terry Fox Library and 425 underground parking stalls — within walking distance of the downtown lot fabric.

Flood infrastructure is mid-upgrade right now (2026–2027). The City's Cedar Drainage Pump Station project, in the dike system at the northeast end of the city, runs construction summer 2026 to summer 2027 with completion expected late summer 2027 — a dated, sourced constraint on low-ground lots.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Central Port Coquitlam
What a duplex looks like in Central Port Coquitlam

items.t: The usual duplex form: Zoning Bylaw No. 3630 sets apartment zones RA1 / RA2 concentrated downtown and along main roads, townhouse zones RTh1, RTh2 and RTh3, a rowhouse zone RRh, and single-detached zones RS1 through RS4 (minimum lot widths RS1 at least 15 m, RS2 at least 12 m, RS3 at least 30 m, RS4 at least 9.5 m); RS-zoned lots across the city can hold 3 to 6 small-scale multi-unit housing units without rezoning, depending on lot size, location and transit proximity, and secondary suite rules apply.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Central Port Coquitlam

items.t: The two-unit / row form runs through the rowhouse zone RRh, the townhouse zones RTh1–RTh3 and the RS1–RS4 single-detached zones (with suites / SSMUH below); apartment zones RA1 (FAR 1.0, increasable to 1.5 with required parking underground / in structure, further to 2.0 on a $50/sq ft amenity contribution) and RA2 (FAR up to 2.5) govern the downtown apartment form, not duplexes. The zone for a specific lot is read off the current Bylaw 3630 text for that lot.

SSMUH position (City position): RS-zoned lots across the city can hold 3 to 6 small-scale multi-unit housing units without rezoning, depending on lot size, location and transit proximity. That is the City's own published range, stated as the City states it — duplexes are the baseline two-unit form within it.

faq.a: No — there is no SkyTrain station inside Port Coquitlam; the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension is at Coquitlam Central, the West Coast Express stops at Port Coquitlam Station in this sub-area, and an extension is an exploratory business case only (Mayors' Council Feb 19, 2026 work plan) — no funding, route or dates to price.
faq.q: Does Port Coquitlam have a SkyTrain station?

faq.a: A significant portion of the city, including low-lying central land, is within the Fraser and Pitt River floodplain and protected by dyke infrastructure, per the City — check the specific lot.
faq.q: Is Central Port Coquitlam in a floodplain?

faq.a: SD43 catchments are address-based. The one locator run on record for this sub-area (2150 Wilson Ave) returned Central Community Elementary, École Pitt River Middle and École Riverside Secondary — that result belongs to that address only; run the exact address before promising a school.
faq.q: Which schools serve a downtown lot?

faq.a: The duplex / row picture is the form class: RRh rowhouses, RTh townhouses and RS lots holding suites or 3–6 SSMUH units, house by house.
faq.q: Is there a named duplex complex in downtown PoCo?

faq.a: No — Port Coquitlam Station is West Coast Express (weekday peak-direction).
Form B diligence in full — and a 2-lot strata is below the 5-lot depreciation-report threshold, so ask what reports actually exist.
faq.q: If I buy half of a strata duplex, what diligence applies?

faq.a: Much of it is — low-lying central land sits in the Fraser / Pitt River floodplain behind dykes. Check the specific lot with the City.
